title: Header section links are full document loads; the shell unmounts on every switch
body:
## Summary
HeaderBar draws every built section as a plain <a href>, so each nav click reloads the whole document and remounts the shell.

## Description
app/(studio)/_shell/HeaderBar.tsx:53 renders `<a href={x.href}>` while the brand (HeaderBar.tsx:41) uses next/link. The plain anchor dates from Phase 1 (f3a99718) when Projects and Library were v1 routes outside the world (nav.ts header, corrected in c22d888c); since Phase 6 wave C every section is a (studio) route. Each switch re-runs Providers (keymap install, identity check, onIdTokenChanged subscription -> one POST /api/session, session.ts:45), reopens the SSE feed and re-renders the layout's principal check, and drops the toast. Violates app-shell golden path 'The shell never unmounts' (frame continuity). Fixed: `<Link href prefetch={false}>` for built sections (prefetch off so eight sections are not rendered on every page load; the Floor walks every v1 store).

## Flow
- operator clicks Library from the Floor -> browser document load -> Providers mount -> POST /api/session + new EventSource
- proposal: swap the anchor for Link prefetch={false}; keep the unbuilt branch; re-measure

## Expected impact
Every section switch stops paying a document load, a session POST and a stream reopen; risk: a page that relied on a full load to reset module state (the Board @sheet slot keeps its last page on soft nav, Board.tsx:66-74 already handles that).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer document loads and session POSTs per section switch
Before: 1 document load + 1 POST /api/session + 1 new EventSource per header click (code read; HeaderBar.tsx:53, Providers.tsx:84)
After: predicted 0 / 0 / 0 (stream reopen only where the target page opens one)
Method: simulation - the live lane is the instrument and agents may not run it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/_shell/HeaderBar.tsx:53 <a href={x.href} aria-current=...>
app/(studio)/_shell/HeaderBar.tsx:41 <Link className={s.brand} href="/floor">
git log -S'<a href={x.href}' -> f3a99718, 47b8095b
instrument: tests/live: count `page.on('load')` and POST /api/session across Floor -> Library -> Ledger header clicks on both arms

title: The session cookie is re-posted on every shell mount, and twice on a first visit
body:
## Summary
subscribeSessionCookie posts on Firebase's initial onIdTokenChanged callback, so every shell mount POSTs /api/session even when the server just verified this cookie; the handoff posts the same token again.

## Description
app/(studio)/_shell/session.ts:45-55 posts on every callback; Firebase fires the listener once on subscribe with the current user. Providers.tsx:84 subscribes on mount, and HeaderBar's full document loads (see the nav card) make every section switch a mount. On a first visit Handoff.tsx:35-37 posts and then router.refresh renders Providers, which posts again. Fixed: skip the subscription's first callback when the layout handed Providers a known identity, so only rotations post.

## Flow
- page load with a valid gt_session -> layout principal ok -> Providers mount -> onIdTokenChanged initial fire -> POST /api/session (redundant)
- proposal: pass `identity !== null` into subscribeSessionCookie and drop the initial callback

## Expected impact
One fewer verified POST per page load; risk: a token Firebase refreshed while the tab was closed reaches the server only at the next rotation (the cookie still lives its own token's life).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - session POSTs per page load
Before: 1 per mount, 2 on a first visit (code read)
After: predicted 0 per mount, 1 on a first visit
Method: simulation - needs firebase/auth mocked under vitest (vi.mock), not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/_shell/session.ts:47 return onIdTokenChanged(authClient(), (user) => { ... postSession
app/(studio)/_shell/Providers.tsx:84 useEffect(() => subscribeSessionCookie(...), [])
app/(studio)/_shell/Handoff.tsx:37 .then(postSession)
instrument: vitest: vi.mock('firebase/auth') with an onIdTokenChanged that fires immediately; count fetch('/api/session') per subscribe on both arms

title: where_am_i names the page under the Board sheet, not the packet on screen
body:
## Summary
An agent's open /board/<packet> (soft navigation) answers the heading of the page beneath the Board sheet, because the heading is read only inside main#content.

## Description
AgentNav.tsx:36 reads `main#content h1`; the Board sheet is the layout's `sheet` slot, drawn beside main (layout.tsx:182) as a LevelSheet role=dialog aria-label={name} (packages/ui/src/components/sheet/LevelSheet.tsx:59-61). `arrive` (AgentNav.tsx:45) is satisfied because main still holds the old page. So `open /board/pkt:spend:2026-10-24` from the Floor reports heading 'Floor'. Also AgentNav.tsx:48 says 'not on screen after 20 s' when the bridge aborted the call early. Fixed: prefer an open `[role=dialog][aria-label]` over main's heading, and an abort answers 'cancelled'.

## Flow
- agent: open /board/pkt:spend:<day> while on /floor -> router.push -> sheet draws -> here() -> heading 'Floor'
- proposal: heading() checks the sheet dialog first; arrive distinguishes abort from timeout

## Expected impact
The agent reads the packet it opened; risk: a page's own dialog (Compose) would be named while open, which is also what is on screen.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - heading reported matches the surface on screen
Before: 0 of 1 Board-sheet arrivals named the packet (code walk)
After: predicted 1 of 1
Method: simulation - no DOM in the vitest rung (no jsdom/happy-dom installed); athena-portable's live journey is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/live (or athena-portable journey): open /board/<fixture packet> from /floor through document.modelContext, assert heading equals the sheet's name
drain_note: instrument could not draw the sheet via router.push

title: The handoff draws nothing when the server set the cookie and the next request still lacks it
body:
## Summary
After a successful POST /api/session the handoff refreshes once; if the browser dropped the cookie the layout renders the same Handoff, whose effect does not re-run, and the screen stays blank with no error.

## Description
Handoff.tsx:41 router.refresh() on ok; the effect's deps (authResolved, user, router) do not change, so a second refusal from the layout (layout.tsx:167-171) leaves `refusal` null and Handoff returns null (Handoff.tsx:53). Reproducible: app/_server/session.ts:56 marks the cookie Secure on any non-loopback host, so a studio reached over LAN http (http://192.168.x.x:3000) gets a cookie the browser refuses. Fixed: after the refresh, a second render still without a principal shows an ErrorLine with the facts (the server set gt_session; the next request arrived without it).

## Flow
- open the studio over LAN http, signed in -> 401 -> Handoff posts -> 200 + Secure cookie dropped -> refresh -> 401 -> Handoff (same instance) -> blank screen

## Expected impact
The operator sees why the studio will not open instead of an empty page; risk: a slow refresh read as a failure if the bound is too short.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a dropped session cookie is a shown error, not a blank screen
Before: blank screen, 0 lines (code walk of the three files)
After: predicted one ErrorLine
Method: simulation - needs a browser on a non-loopback http origin
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/live against the dev server bound to a LAN address over http: sign in with a fixture token, assert an ErrorLine within N s

title: Which pile sources are the scout's is spelled three times
body:
## Summary
The scout/seeds source set lives in facts.ts SCOUT_PILE_SOURCES, nav.ts sectionOf's regex and scout/_scout/ScoutHead.tsx isScoutPacket, with nothing holding them together.

## Description
app/(studio)/_shell/facts.ts:43 Set(['scout','seeds']); app/(studio)/_shell/nav.ts:44 /(scout|seeds)/; app/(studio)/scout/_scout/ScoutHead.tsx:20 source === 'scout' || 'seeds'. facts.ts's own comment says they are the same set. A new scout wing source added to one leaves the Scout header's NEXT, the nav's current mark and the Board's scout packets disagreeing. Fixed: nav.ts and ScoutHead.tsx read SCOUT_PILE_SOURCES (both client-safe), or a test asserts the three agree.

## Flow
- add a source 'scout-reels' to ScoutHead only -> its packets draw as Scout's on /scout, the header marks no section, the Scout NEXT ignores its piles

## Expected impact
One spelling; risk: nav.ts gains an import from facts.ts (types-only today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - spellings of one rule
Before: 3 sites, 0 tests binding them
After: 1 site (or 3 with a binding test)
Method: probe - grep of the three literals
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: for each of the three, the set of sources it accepts equals SCOUT_PILE_SOURCES (seeded red by adding a source to one)

title: A failed sign-out or eviction is a 3.4-second toast and then nothing
body:
## Summary
'sign-out incomplete - ...' and 'storage - ...' go through the same receipt queue as success receipts and close after TOAST_MS, leaving no trace on screen or elsewhere.

## Description
Providers.tsx:106 and :80 call showToast; toast.ts:27-30 closes every receipt after 3400 ms. A sign-out whose DELETE failed leaves the server cookie valid for up to an hour while the page stays put (Providers.tsx:105-108); an identity flip whose eviction failed leaves the previous person's keys. Both are the outcomes most needing evidence and both leave none once the toast fades. Fixed: a failure receipt stays until dismissed (or the shell holds it as an ErrorLine).

## Flow
- sign out with /api/session unreachable -> Firebase signs out, cookie stays -> toast 3.4 s -> page still signed in, no visible reason

## Expected impact
The operator sees that sign-out did not finish; risk: a sticky receipt that is never dismissed covers the toast region.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed privileged act stays visible
Before: visible 3.4 s, 0 durable traces (code read)
After: predicted visible until dismissed
Method: simulation - needs a Toast API for sticky receipts (@gt/ui, outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest on toast.ts: a receipt marked failure stays open past TOAST_MS (shell-toast.test.ts extends)
drain_note: needs a dismiss control in Toast.tsx; shared surface

title: Kit has no door below 1180 px and the spend none below 760 px
body:
## Summary
Shell.module.css hides the kit link at <=1180 px and the spend chip at <=760 px; the nav excludes Kit, so one of eight built sections is unreachable from the header on a tablet or phone.

## Description
app/(studio)/_shell/Shell.module.css:47 `.kitLink{display:none}` at max-width 1180; :54 `.slotSpend{display:none}` at 760; HeaderBar.tsx:37 pages excludes kit. The CSS comment records it as a choice ('the kit link gives way'). Whether Kit belongs on a phone is the operator's call.

## Flow
- open /floor at 1024 px -> no Kit entry anywhere in the header

## Expected impact
Kit reachable at every width, or the choice confirmed; risk: the phone nav scrolls one more entry.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - sections reachable from the header per width
Before: 7 of 8 at <=1180 px
After: 8 of 8 if Kit joins the scrolling nav
Method: probe - CSS read at the three breakpoints
Result: better
Gate: direction
